I think the best would be to update core comfy to natively support webp/gif/whatever animated previews, and then all nodes and projects can uniformly send animated previews in a simple way and all be intercompatible.

The animated preview code is by @AustinMroz, so maybe he can chime in about that, I won't claim to understand how it all works (though it has always worked without any issues for me), I'm simply using it and borrowed his code to test the tiny VAE for previews. 

The VAEs for video are still in beta stage, which is probably why comfy doesn't support it natively yet, and my way of using it is far from perfect too, while it works it has some playback syncing issues currently.

> We could maybe try importing one of the Swarm specific nodes in try/except block, and set the what to send based on if that fails or succeeds.

The problem is that there are two ways to run ComfyUI workflows within SwarmUI. Either directly from within the ComfyUI workflow tab, or from the Generate/Simple tabs. The former works just as Comfy usually does, thus relying on VHS for animated previews, whereas the latter executes the workflow via the Comfy API, requiring this separate preview system. The Swarm nodes are available in both environments, so if we used that method, previews would be broken in the ComfyUI tab.

One of the major goals of my preview code was to not waste time decoding a frame unless it's possible for the frame to be displayed and to seamlessly transition to using new frames as they are available. I left a bit of a breadcrumb trail in the commit logs for VHS, but I did performance testing on 3 or 4 different implementations and found the current to be both fastest and most reliable. I also needed to be a little heavy handed in ensuring that my extension code included a workaround for a [race condition](/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/pull/6124) in native that isn't relevant unless you require ordered output of previews.

It's quite possible the the higher frame rates provided by decoders like TAEHV swing performance away from my current implementation, but I'm a bit too short on time right now to dig into the SwarmUI implementation to do performance testing or see if it includes logic to handle this case.

I've modified it to only encode/send Swarm previews if the Swarm nodes are available, but still send VHS previews either way. That should remove the (tiny) performance cost for non-Swarm users. Also increased the quality of the Swarm previews to 80 because 50 was extremely blocky.

title: Load clip vision models from the `clip_vision` folder.
body:
I first brought this topic up in #177 and part of your response was:

> it's true now it'd make more sense in the clip_vision folder, but I didn't want to change it as many people already had things setup.

Having now spent some weeks using it I can say that I'm somewhat annoyed in having to move my clip vision models around based on which nodes I'm using - as these models are usually expected to be in the `clip_vision` folder but the `LoadWanVideoClipTextEncoder` node expects them to be in the `text_encoders` folder for legacy reasons that  you mentioned in #177.

So with this PR I propose a solution. By default we expect the models to be in the `clip_vision` folder in order to achieve greater compatability with the larger ComfyUI community. However under the hood we will also still support loading the models from the `text_encoders` folder so that the people who have already set up their workflows won't experience any disruptions. Things will keep working for them.
author: xStrom

comments.body:
I don't understand what you mean by moving models around, what other node even can use the roberta clip model? 

You can already use the normal comfyui clip vision loader and the same clip vit h model the native workflows use, and those are naturally loaded from the clip vision folder.

The `clip_vision_h` isn't `fp32` though. As for the nodes, I use the one in this repo and various forks of it that use the `clip_vision` folder.

You yourself mentioned that the `clip_vision` folder makes more sense and that the problem is not wanting to break existing setups. I think the PR here addresses that concern.

Are there other concerns why you wouldn't want it to be `clip_vision` by default, with backwards compatible support for `text_encoders`?

Just in general never tried to do it like this... won't this still force people to move the models and only address the case where old workflow had it already selected?

And the case where workflow is shared and the user has to re-select the model if their path doesn't match, for example loading workflow saved in Windows on Linux, and vice versa.. or using subfolders.

As work around go it's better than nothing sure, still wondering if it would be better to just allow loading from both folders in this node? Assuming that's doable, never tried, I'd imagine it would work if we get list of both folder and join it.

Yes, the current solution is designed to direct people towards using the `clip_vision` directory. So selecting will only show models from `clip_vision`.

My thinking was that most people who have an existing setup don't really choose between different models anymore. They already chose either the `fp16` or `fp32` version and that selection will continue working.

The saved value is just the model file name. So sharing workflows (to other users, or between Windows/Linux) will work fine as long as the file name matches. One setup can have `open-clip-xlm-roberta-large-vit-huge-14_visual_fp32.safetensors` in `clip_vision` and another setup in `text_encoders`. Both setups can use the same workflow file just fine.

However let's say someone shares a workflow with `open-clip-xlm-roberta-large-vit-huge-14_visual_fp32.safetensors` but the receiving user has renamed their file to `foobar-clip.safetensors`. Well yes, now they need to select that, and to do that with this PR they need to move that file to `clip_vision` to be able to select it.

Now it is possible to allow selecting models from `text_encoders` as well. Here are the pros and cons:

### Allow selecting from both `clip_vision` and `text_encoders`

\+ Those who want to keep switching between `fp16` and `fp32` can continue to do so without moving the models to `clip_vision`.
\+ If someone receives a shared workflow with a mismatching model name, they can use the selection UI to select from the `text_encoders` folder.
\- The selection choices for everyone contain irrelevant models like `umt5-xxl-enc-bf16.safetensors`, making the selection more confusing.

### Allow selecting only from `clip_vision`, but support loading any previously made selection from `text_encoders`

\+ The selection choices contain only clip vision models, reducing noise in the UI.
\- Those who want to keep switching between `fp16` and `fp32` need to move their models to `clip_vision`.
\- Those who receive shared workflows with mismatching model names need to move their models to `clip_vision` in order to select them.

---

So basically the choice comes down to what to optimize for.

Do you want the selection experience to be less noisy (no `umt5-xxl-enc-bf16.safetensors` etc) for everyone at the cost of some more active users needing to move their clip models to `clip_vision`?

or

Do you want the selection to continue working for absolutely everyone at the cost of keeping the UI noisy for everyone?

---

In this PR I chose to optimize for less UI noise. The thinking is that most users haven't still downloaded this - people are still finding out Wan 2.1 even exists. Then, most users who already have it set up won't be changing the selected model. Those users who will be changing the model are likely to be smart enough to figure out that they need to move the models to `clip_vision`.

title: Add validation and documentation to VAE tiling.
body:
Like I mentioned in #350 I got an error with VAE tiling since the latest fix in 0cf1330928512397134201ac192597466b3a2198. This motivated me to actually read the code in `nodes.py` and `wan_video_vae.py` to understand how this tiling is supposed to work. Now that I have a better understanding of how it works it makes sense to also improve the documentation for VAE tiling so that others can get a better grasp on this without having to dig through the code themselves.

---

First, there are a couple of rules that need to be upheld. Currently failing to follow these rules will cause an error at the end of running the workflow, just when the VAE tiling is supposed to happen. In this PR I added a validation check to error out at the beginning so that people don't waste time trying to run bad settings.

The first rule is that the tile size can't be smaller than the tile stride size. This is fundamentally expected in `wan_video_vae.py` where if the tile size is smaller, that difference will just be skipped completely - which is clearly not good behavior.

```python
for h in range(0, H, stride_h):
    if (h-stride_h >= 0 and h-stride_h+size_h >= H): continue
    for w in range(0, W, stride_w):
        if (w-stride_w >= 0 and w-stride_w+size_w >= W): continue
        h_, w_ = h + size_h, w + size_w
        tasks.append((h, h_, w, w_))
```

The second rule is that the tile size can't be equal to the stride size either. I'm not sure this is a fundamental requirement, but it is a de facto requirement of `wan_video_vae.py` right now. Using an equal tile size and stride size will just result in an error, e.g. `The expanded size of the tensor (160) must match the existing size (0) at non-singleton dimension 0.`

Thus to satisfy both of these rules we need to make sure that the tile size is always larger than the stride size. This PR adds a `VALIDATE_INPUTS` class method to make sure this is true before the workflow execution starts.

---

Both the tile size and stride size in pixels are expected by the code to be a multiple of 8. This PR adjusts the `step` on the node inputs to match the UI with this backend reality.

---

I rewrote the tooltips to add more detailed info based on my new understanding from reading the code and from inspecting a bunch of tiled test runs.

The key points are:
* Seams will definitely happen, it's just a question of how many and how obviously visible they are.
* The stride size determines the number and location of seams.
* The tile size determines how obviously visible the seams are. I found that a tile size of 1.5x stride already achieves invisibility for a quick glance and that 2x stride is barely noticable - requiring me to really zoom in at known seam location coordinates.

---

Closes #350
